title: Reverse Bits
description:
# Reverse Bits

Reverse the bits of a given 32-bit integer and return the resulting 32-bit pattern as a Java `int`.

In Java there is no unsigned `int` return type. If the reversed pattern has the sign bit set, the displayed decimal result is the signed two's-complement value for that same 32-bit pattern. The operation is about the raw 32 bits, not about decimal digits or string characters.

Negative values also have exactly 32 bits. For example, `-1` has 32 one bits; `-3` has pattern `11111111111111111111111111111101`.

## Example 1:

**Input:** n = 43261596
**Output:** 964176192
**Explanation:** The bit pattern `00000010100101000001111010011100` reverses to `00111001011110000010100101000000`.

## Example 2:

**Input:** n = -3
**Output:** -1073741825
**Explanation:** The input bit pattern is `11111111111111111111111111111101`. Reversing it gives `10111111111111111111111111111111`, which is unsigned `3221225471` but signed Java int `-1073741825`.

## Constraints:

* `n` is treated as one 32-bit integer value.

solutions.name: Bit-by-Bit Shift Accumulator
solutions.description:
## Approach
Build the answer one bit at a time. Shift the result left, append the current lowest bit of `n`, then move `n` right with the unsigned shift operator. Repeat exactly 32 times so leading zeros are preserved.

## Key Insight
The first bit read from the input must become the highest bit of the output. A left-shifting accumulator naturally creates that order, and `>>>` is required so negative inputs expose their raw bit pattern instead of extending the sign bit.

## Complexity Analysis
Time Complexity: O(32), which is O(1) for fixed-width integers. Space Complexity: O(1).

solutions.name: Mask Swap Divide and Conquer
solutions.description:
## Approach
Swap progressively smaller groups of bits with masks: adjacent bits, 2-bit groups, nibbles, bytes, and finally 16-bit halves. After these fixed stages, every bit has moved to its mirrored position.

## Key Insight
Bit reversal can be seen as repeated symmetric exchanges at different scales. The masks isolate alternating groups, and unsigned shifts keep the high bits from being filled by sign extension.

## Complexity Analysis
Time Complexity: O(1), because the number of masks is fixed. Space Complexity: O(1).

solutions.name: Byte Lookup Table
solutions.description:
## Approach
Precompute the reversed-bit value for every byte from `0` to `255`. Split the 32-bit input into four bytes, reverse each byte through the table, and reassemble them in opposite byte order.

## Key Insight
The same 8-bit reversal subproblem appears repeatedly. A fixed 256-entry table is still constant space here and is useful when many values are reversed by the same solution instance.

## Complexity Analysis
Time Complexity: O(1). Space Complexity: O(1), because the lookup table has fixed size.

solutions.name: Opposite Mask Assembly
solutions.description:
## Approach
Keep two masks: one scans the source from the lowest bit upward, and the other writes into the result from the highest bit downward. When a source bit is set, set the mirrored target bit.

## Key Insight
This version makes the mapping between positions explicit: bit `i` in the input maps to bit `31 - i` in the output. It avoids shifting the input value itself and is a useful contrast to the accumulator method.

## Complexity Analysis
Time Complexity: O(32), which is O(1) for one fixed-width integer. Space Complexity: O(1).

solutions.name: Recursive Half Reversal
solutions.description:
## Approach
Define a helper that reverses only the lowest `width` bits of a value. Split the range into low and high halves, recursively reverse both halves, then place the reversed low half before the reversed high half.

## Key Insight
This is the recursive form of divide and conquer. Reversal swaps the two halves and reverses each half internally, which mirrors the same structure used by the iterative mask-swap solution.

## Complexity Analysis
Time Complexity: O(32), because each bit participates in a constant number of recursive levels for a fixed-width integer. Space Complexity: O(1), since the recursion depth is fixed at five levels.

tests.description: Canonical positive bit pattern reverses to another positive int.
Negative signed input represents an unsigned bit pattern whose reversed result is also signed.
Lowest bit set moves to the sign bit after reversal.
Only the sign bit set moves down to the lowest bit.
All-one bit pattern remains all ones.
Second lowest bit moves near the top after reversal.
Third lowest bit moves to the corresponding high position.
Another low single-bit value checks position arithmetic.
Largest positive int reverses to all ones except the lowest bit.
Alternating 0101 bits reverse into alternating 1010 bits.
Alternating 1010 bits reverse back into alternating 0101 bits.
